diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given $z_1^n \in [0, 1]$ and $\Delta t_{\mathrm{im}} > 0$, the updated volume fraction $z_1^{n+1}$ determined by the implicit scheme

issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies the intermediate value theorem to F(z) = (z - z1^n)/dt - f(z) on [0,1], which requires f (hence kappa^{n+1}) to be defined and continuous on all of [0,1]; this premise is asserted without justification and is false in general. For the Tammann EOS with p_{w,1} != p_{w,2} (the gas-liquid case, e.g. p_{w,1}=0, p_{w,2}=6000), kappa^{n+1} = z1 z2 (nu1 - nu2)/(z1 nu1 + z2 nu2) with nu_k = 1/(gamma_k (p^{n+1}(z)+p_{w,k})) and p^{n+1}(z) = ((rho e)^n - B(z))/A(z) has poles in (0,1): when p^{n+1}(z) lies between -p_{w,2} and -p_{w,1}, nu_1 and nu_2 have opposite signs and z1 nu1 + z2 nu2 vanishes at some z* in (0,1) while the numerator stays nonzero. This occurs even for admissible data in G^p: with gamma_1=1.4, p_{w,1}=0, gamma_2=4.4, p_{w,2}=6000 and state z1^n=0.99, rho_1=rho_2=1, u=0, E=100 (so p^n is about 9 > 0), p^{n+1}(z) < 0 for z < 0.987 and kappa^{n+1} has a pole at z* around 0.39; taking D_h = div u^n = -1 and dt_im = 1 gives F < 0 on [0,z*) and F > 0 on (z*,1], so F = 0 has no solution in [0,1]: the conclusion fails within the stated hypotheses. (For p_{w,1} = p_{w,2}, e.g. gas-gas with p_w = 0, kappa extends continuously and the argument works; the failure is specific to the gas-liquid Tammann regime that is the paper's headline application.) Such poles are present throughout gas-rich regions of the paper's own water-air tests (there rho e is about 2.5, so p^{n+1}(z) < 0 for most z in [0,1]), and the proposed bisection can converge to a pole and return a spurious z1^{n+1}.

failure_location.quote: The continuity of $F(z_1)$ guarantees the existence of root $z_1^{n+1} \in [0, 1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add hypotheses ensuring f is well defined and continuous on [0,1] (e.g. that (rho e)^n keeps p^{n+1}(z) + p_{w,k} > 0 for all z in [0,1]) so the IVT argument applies, and correspondingly weaken the unconditional claim; this excludes gas-rich mixture states that occur in the paper's own gas-liquid simulations. Alternatively, redesign the implicit evaluation of kappa^{n+1} and re-prove BP. No repair preserves the unconditional statement in the gas-liquid Tammann regime.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional BP guarantee of the implicit kappa-solver (Theorem thm:implicit_solver), the BP property asserted for the adaptive backward-Euler/SDIRK2 strategy (adaptive_sdirk2, whose proof is omitted as 'similar'), and the abstract/introduction/conclusion claims of a rigorously proved unconditional BP property all become unreliable; the bisection step is also not guaranteed to return a bounded solution.
issues.title: Implicit kappa-solver BP theorem rests on a false continuity premise; existence of a solution in [0,1] can fail
issues.why_classification: The statement is false within its stated hypotheses, the counterexample lies in the advertised gas-liquid regime, and the failure arises for large time steps - exactly the regime the implicit solver is meant to unlock; every supported repair excludes an advertised regime or withdraws the central unconditional guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 2 damps the solution toward the cell average with a factor theta_p obtained by linear interpolation in the pressure alone. Along the segment U(theta) = Ubar + theta(Utilde - Ubar), the mixture pressure equals N(theta)/A(theta), where N (internal energy minus the linear background term, cf. the proof of thm:convex_Gp) is concave and A(theta) = sum_l z_l(theta)/(gamma_l - 1) is linear but nonconstant; concavity yields p >= epsilon_p only for theta <= A(Ubar)(p(Ubar)-eps_p) / [A(Ubar)(p(Ubar)-eps_p) - A(Utilde)(p(Utilde)-eps_p)], which is strictly smaller than the paper's theta_p whenever the quadrature point is more gas-rich than the average (A(Utilde) > A(Ubar), gamma_1 < gamma_2). Concrete failure with zero velocity (where the concavity bound is exact): gamma_1=1.4, p_{w,1}=0, gamma_2=4.4, p_{w,2}=6000, Ubar = (0.5, 0.5, 0, 3883.75, 0.5) with p(Ubar) about 1, quadrature value Utilde = (0.9, 0.1, 0, 700, 0.9) with p = -33.5; then theta_p is about 0.029, but the limited state Ubar + theta_p(Utilde - Ubar) has p about -0.60 < epsilon_p, so the limiter does not restore pressure positivity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace theta_p by the concavity-based threshold, e.g. the minimum over violating quadrature points q of A(Ubar)(p(Ubar)-eps_p) / [A(Ubar)(p(Ubar)-eps_p) - A(Utilde(q))(p(Utilde(q))-eps_p)] (or solve N(theta) = eps_p A(theta) exactly), and justify it by concavity of N - eps_p A as in the proof of thm:convex_Gp; the scheme, the limiter structure, and the guarantee then survive unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee that the BP-limited solution lies in G^p at all Gauss-Lobatto points is false as written, so the pressure-positivity component of the BP-OEDG guarantee (abstract, Section 4.2.1, conclusion) is not delivered by the limiter.
issues.title: BP limiter pressure-scaling factor is incorrect for the mixture Tammann EOS
issues.why_classification: A contained correction of one formula plus a short concavity argument restores the full guarantee with no change to the scheme or its scope, but it is a genuine mathematical repair of an incorrect construction rather than a typo.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, enforce the pressure positivity $p \geq \varepsilon_p$ with $\varepsilon_p = \min\{ p(\overline{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j}^n), 10^{-13} \}$.
complemented by a BP limiter to ensure the BP property of partial densities, pressure, and volume fraction

issues.failure_explanation: The claim that the BP limiter guarantees membership in G^p at the quadrature points presupposes that each cell average Ubar_{i,j}^n itself lies in G^p after the DG/SSP-RK updates of the transport step: the tolerances are built from the averages (eps_l = min{(z_l rho_l)-bar, 1e-13}, eps_p = min{p(Ubar), 1e-13}) and the theta-formulas divide by quantities such as p(Ubar) - min p, which degenerate or become meaningless if p(Ubar) <= 0. The paper proves convexity of G^p (thm:convex_Gp) but never states, proves, or cites a cell-average admissibility result for its Lax-Friedrichs-flux DG update on the new set G^p (cited prior works use G), and no CFL condition for average preservation is given. The overall BP guarantee is therefore unsupported as written: if an average leaves G^p, the limiter is undefined or ineffective.

failure_location.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a cell-average BP lemma for the transport step (SSP-RK with the Lax-Friedrichs flux keeps Ubar_{i,j} in G^p under an explicit CFL bound, using the convexity established in thm:convex_Gp), or add average admissibility explicitly as a standing hypothesis; the scheme and limiter are otherwise unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The headline bound-preserving guarantee of the BP-OEDG scheme for partial densities, pressure, and volume fraction (abstract, Section 4.2.1, conclusion) lacks its required premise; without it the limiter cannot deliver the advertised bounds.
issues.title: BP guarantee presupposes admissible cell averages, which are never established
issues.why_classification: The missing ingredient is a contained but genuinely new lemma (or an explicitly added hypothesis); with it all stated guarantees survive, but as written the central BP claim does not follow from the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where a 1.22 Mach number shock wave hits a helium bubble

issues.failure_explanation: For pre-shock air (rho_1, p_1) = (1.4, 1e5) with gamma_1 = 1.4, the post-shock density 1.92691 and pressure 1.5698e5 are exactly the Mach-1.22 shock values, but the Rankine-Hugoniot relations then fix the post-shock velocity: mass and momentum give shock speed |D| = sqrt(rho_2 (p_2 - p_1)/(rho_1 (rho_2 - rho_1))) is approximately 385.7 and u_2 = -|D|(1 - rho_1/rho_2) is approximately -105.4, not -113.5. (The value 113.5 corresponds to a standard-air sound speed of about 340, i.e. rho_1 about 1.21, a different unit convention.) The given post-shock state is therefore not a consistent shock for the stated pre-shock state; alternatively, with u_2 = -113.5 the mass relation forces a shock speed of about -414.8, which violates momentum conservation by about 9 percent. The initial condition does not represent the claimed clean Mach-1.22 shock and produces spurious transients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the post-shock velocity to the Rankine-Hugoniot value of about -105.4 (or rescale the pre-shock state consistently) and rerun the case; all qualitative conclusions are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The air-helium shock-bubble test does not compute the stated configuration; quantitative details of that experiment (effective shock strength and speed, the timing of the 62-983 microsecond comparisons with the Haas-Sturtevant experiment) are unreliable.
issues.title: Air-helium shock-bubble post-shock state violates the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions
issues.why_classification: A single inconsistent datum with a forced Rankine-Hugoniot correction; the method, all guarantees, and the qualitative experimental conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal G=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ c^2(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}

issues.failure_explanation: G requires strict positivity of both partial densities. U^{(1)} = (1.2, 0, 0, 1000, 1) has z_2 rho_2 = 0 and U^{(2)} = (0, 1000, 0, 6001, 0) has z_1 rho_1 = 0, so neither state belongs to G as defined; the membership assertions in Appendix A are false, and the exhibited pair therefore does not, as written, demonstrate non-convexity of G. (The conclusion is salvageable - the two states lie in the closure of G while their midpoint has c^2 < 0 and thus lies outside the closure, and convexity of G would imply convexity of its closure - but this argument is not given.)

failure_location.quote: Thus, $\mathbf{U}^{(1)}$ is physically admissible and belongs to $\mathcal{G}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perturb the endpoint states to have z_k rho_k = epsilon > 0 and re-verify membership and the mixed-state failure, or replace the false membership assertions by the closure argument (the states lie in the closure of G, their midpoint does not, hence G is non-convex).
issues.overall_effect: The claim (Section 2 and Appendix A) that a concrete counterexample demonstrates non-convexity of G is unsupported as written, weakening the motivation for introducing G^p; thm:convex_Gp itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Appendix A counterexample uses endpoint states outside the defined admissible set G
issues.why_classification: A short local repair (perturbation of the two states or a few-line closure argument) preserves the non-convexity claim in full; no substantive result is lost.
